components: C1 (0-20): First-party, single build tool that is the de-facto standard for the whole ecosystem
C2 (0-20): Native unit + integration test runner invoked by the same tool, zero extra install
C3 (0-20): Native support for executable/verified documentation examples as part of the standard test run
C5 (0-20): Maturity of benchmark + coverage tooling reachable from the standard build tool (native or one-command-away, widely standardized)
rubric.description: Frozen rubric applied identically to all 10 languages (this shard scores Rust only). Five equally-weighted (20 pts each) sub-components measuring build-system/test-framework integration maturity, independent of intrinsic language diagnostics (scored under Language Quality).
sources: doc.rust-lang.org/cargo (Cargo Book, cargo test / cargo bench command references)

C1_build_tool.note: Cargo ships with the toolchain and is the single, universal build tool for essentially all Rust projects; no competing first-party or de-facto alternative exists.

C2_test_runner.citation: Compile and execute unit, integration, and documentation tests.
C2_test_runner.note: cargo test compiles and runs unit tests, and separately-located integration tests, natively.

C3_doc_tests.citation: For documentation tests, the working directory when invoking rustdoc is set to the workspace root directory
C3_doc_tests.note: Doc comments containing fenced code blocks are compiled and executed by the same 'cargo test' invocation used for unit/integration tests, giving Rust a distinctive built-in living-documentation test integration that most peer languages lack natively.

C4_workspaces.citation: Workspaces allow you to manage multiple related packages together.
C4_workspaces.note: Cargo workspaces let cargo test/--workspace build and test all member crates together, sharing a lockfile and target directory.

C5_bench_coverage.citation: The #[bench] attribute is currently unstable and only available on the nightly channel.
C5_bench_coverage.note: cargo bench exists but its libtest #[bench] harness remains unstable/nightly-only on the officially shipped toolchain; the stable-channel path requires the third-party Criterion crate. Code coverage likewise has no first-party 'cargo coverage' command and instead relies on the well-established but external cargo-llvm-cov / cargo-tarpaulin subcommands wrapping rustc's instrumentation. Deducted points versus a hypothetical fully first-party bench+coverage story.

components: D1 (0-20): First-party API-doc generator integrated into the standard toolchain/build tool
D2 (0-20): Documentation examples are executed/verified as part of routine testing (not merely lint-checked)
D3 (0-20): Centralized, automatic, free hosting of generated API docs for essentially the whole package ecosystem
D4 (0-20): Depth/coverage of official learning material (tutorial book, language reference, style/idiom guides) maintained by the language org
D5 (0-20): Quality/consistency signaling tooling for library authors (missing-doc lints, doc-alias, intra-doc links, badges)
rubric.description: Frozen rubric applied identically to all 10 languages (this shard scores Rust only). Five equally-weighted (20 pts each) sub-components measuring documentation ecosystem maturity, distinct from code-level diagnostics scored under Language Quality.

D1_generator.citation: Build the documentation for the local package and all dependencies.
D1_generator.note: rustdoc ships with the toolchain and is invoked transparently via 'cargo doc'; it produces HTML docs from doc comments and Markdown for every crate with zero extra tooling.

D2_doctests.citation: Every block compiles and runs when you call cargo test.
D2_doctests.note: Code examples inside /// doc comments compile and run as tests under the standard 'cargo test' flow, so published examples are continuously verified, not just rendered.

D3_hosting.citation: All libraries published to crates.io are documented.
D3_hosting.note: docs.rs automatically builds and freely hosts rustdoc output for essentially every library published to crates.io, with no publisher action required beyond 'cargo publish'.

D4_official_material.citation: The following books are maintained at rust-lang.org.
D4_official_material.note: The Rust project maintains an extensive official documentation suite -- 'the book' (The Rust Programming Language), the Reference, Rust by Example, Rustlings, the Cargo Book, the rustdoc Book, the Rustonomicon, and the Style Guide -- all versioned and shipped alongside compiler releases.

D5_quality_tooling.note: rustdoc provides dedicated lints (missing_docs, broken_intra_doc_links, missing_crate_level_docs) and features like #[doc(alias=...)] to help authors keep docs complete and correct, though some of these lints are allow-by-default or nightly-only, so they require deliberate opt-in rather than being enforced out of the box.
